name: list_organizations
title: List Organizations
description: List all organizations the current user belongs to. Supports optional `search` parameter to filter by name or ID.

search.description: Search organizations by name or ID. You can specify partial name or ID values to filter results.

name: run_sql
title: Run SQL
description: Execute one SQL statement on a Neon database. If a prior step created a temporary branch, pass that branch_id. NEVER run destructive SQL autonomously; always ask the user first.

project_id.description: The ID of the project to execute the query against

branch_id.description: An optional ID of the branch to execute the query against. If not provided the default branch is used.

database_name.description: The name of the database. If not provided, the default neondb or first available database is used.

role_name.description: An optional Postgres role to log in as. The server resolves its credentials internally and never returns them. If not provided, the database owner is used. On a connection pinned to a role, omit this or pass that role.

compute_id.description: An optional ID of the compute/endpoint to run on. If not provided, the read-write compute of the branch is used.

max_rows.description: Maximum number of rows to return per statement. When a statement returns more, the response adds a second block with `totalRowCount` and `truncated: true`; raise this only then.

name: run_sql_transaction
title: Run SQL Transaction
description: Execute multiple SQL statements as one transaction. If a prior step created a temporary branch, pass that branch_id. NEVER run destructive SQL autonomously; always ask the user first.

project_id.description: The ID of the project to execute the query against

branch_id.description: An optional ID of the branch to execute the query against. If not provided the default branch is used.

database_name.description: The name of the database. If not provided, the default neondb or first available database is used.

role_name.description: An optional Postgres role to log in as. The server resolves its credentials internally and never returns them. If not provided, the database owner is used. On a connection pinned to a role, omit this or pass that role.

compute_id.description: An optional ID of the compute/endpoint to run on. If not provided, the read-write compute of the branch is used.

max_rows.description: Maximum number of rows to return per statement. When a statement returns more, the response adds a second block with `totalRowCount` and `truncated: true`; raise this only then.

name: describe_table_schema
title: Describe Table Schema
description: Get column definitions, data types, and constraints for a specific table. Do not use when you need all tables in a database (use `get_database_tables` instead).

table_name.description: The table name, optionally schema-qualified (for example, crm.contacts)

project_id.description: The ID of the project to execute the query against

branch_id.description: An optional ID of the branch to execute the query against. If not provided the default branch is used.

database_name.description: The name of the database. If not provided, the default neondb or first available database is used.

name: get_database_tables
title: Get Database Tables
description: List all tables in a Neon database. Do not use when you need column-level detail for a specific table (use `describe_table_schema` instead).

branch_id.description: An optional ID of the branch. If not provided the default branch is used.

database_name.description: The name of the database. If not provided, the default neondb or first available database is used.

name: prepare_database_migration
title: Prepare Database Migration
description: Apply a schema change on a temporary branch and return a migration_id. Test with run_sql on that branch, ask the user, then complete_database_migration — even if they reject, so the temporary branch is deleted. Pass every field from the prepare response.

migration_sql.description: The SQL to execute to create the migration

project_id.description: The ID of the project to execute the query against

database_name.description: The name of the database. If not provided, the default neondb or first available database is used.

name: complete_database_migration
title: Complete Database Migration
description: Apply or discard a prepared migration and delete the temporary branch. NEVER run autonomously; always ask the user first. Pass migration_id, migration_sql, database_name, project_id, temporary_branch_id, and parent_branch_id from prepare_database_migration. Set apply_changes false to discard; omitting it applies the migration.

migration_sql.description: The SQL statements to apply. Pass the exact value from prepare_database_migration.

database_name.description: The database name. Pass the exact value from prepare_database_migration.

project_id.description: The project ID. Pass the exact value from prepare_database_migration.

temporary_branch_id.description: The temporary branch ID to delete after migration.

parent_branch_id.description: The parent branch ID where migration will be applied.

apply_changes.description: Whether to apply the migration. Set to false to just delete the temp branch without applying.

name: describe_branch
title: Describe Branch
description: Get a tree view of all objects in a branch, including databases, schemas, tables, views, and functions. Do not use when you only need table names (use `get_database_tables` instead) or column detail (use `describe_table_schema` instead).

branch_id.description: An ID of the branch to describe

database_name.description: The name of the database. If not provided, the default neondb or first available database is used.

name: get_connection_string
title: Get Connection String
description: Get a PostgreSQL connection string for a Neon database. The branch must have a compute endpoint. `create_project` and `create_branch` do not return one; call this after they succeed. Branch, compute, and database are optional and resolved automatically if not specified; `project_id` follows the connection scope. Requires write access: the connection string carries a privileged role password, so it is unavailable in read-only mode. A read-only caller who needs a DATABASE_URL must copy it from https://console.neon.tech manually.

branch_id.description: The ID or name of the branch. If not provided, the default branch will be used.

compute_id.description: The ID of the compute/endpoint. If not provided, the read-write compute associated with the branch will be used.

database_name.description: The name of the database. If not provided, the default neondb or first available database is used.

role_name.description: The name of the role to connect with. If not provided, the database owner name will be used.

name: get_neon_auth_config
title: Get Neon Auth configuration
description: Read Neon Auth config for a branch: trusted origins, localhost access, email and password, OAuth providers, email provider, the organization, magic link, and phone number plugins, the webhook, and logs export. OAuth and SMTP secrets are redacted as "***redacted***". Requires provision_neon_auth first.

branch_id.description: Branch ID. If omitted, the project default branch is used (same as provision_neon_auth).

name: explain_sql_statement
title: Explain SQL Statement
description: Generate the execution plan for a SQL statement. When `analyze` is true, PostgreSQL executes the statement and any side effects. Use `analyze: false` to inspect a statement without executing it. Never analyze potentially destructive SQL autonomously. Do not use when you need query results (use `run_sql` instead).

project_id.description: The ID of the project to execute the query against

branch_id.description: An optional ID of the branch to execute the query against. If not provided the default branch is used.

database_name.description: The name of the database. If not provided, the default neondb or first available database is used.

analyze.description: Whether to execute the statement with EXPLAIN ANALYZE. Defaults to false because execution may cause side effects.

name: prepare_query_tuning
title: Prepare Query Tuning
description: Analyze a slow query on a temporary branch and return a tuning_id. Apply suggested SQL with run_sql on that branch, re-run explain_sql_statement there, then complete_query_tuning with the tuning_id (not the branch id) — apply_changes true if they accept, omit it or pass false if they reject, so the temporary branch is deleted. Do not use prepare_database_migration.

sql.description: The SQL statement to analyze and tune

database_name.description: The name of the database to execute the query against

project_id.description: The ID of the project to execute the query against

role_name.description: The name of the role to connect with. If not provided, the default role (usually "neondb_owner") will be used.

name: complete_query_tuning
title: Complete Query Tuning
description: Apply or discard query-tuning changes and delete the temporary branch. NEVER run autonomously. Before calling, apply suggested SQL with run_sql on the temporary branch and re-run explain_sql_statement. Pass the tuning_id from prepare_query_tuning, not the branch id, plus temporary_branch_id. Set apply_changes true to apply; omitting it discards. Call this even when the user rejects the changes. Do not use prepare_database_migration.

suggested_sql_statements.description: The SQL DDL statements to execute to improve performance. These statements are the result of the prior steps, for example creating additional indexes.

apply_changes.description: Whether to apply the suggested changes to the main branch

tuning_id.description: The ID of the tuning to complete. This is NOT the branch ID. Remember this ID from the prior step using tool prepare_query_tuning.

database_name.description: The name of the database to execute the query against

project_id.description: The ID of the project to execute the query against

role_name.description: The name of the role to connect with. If you have used a specific role in prepare_query_tuning you MUST pass the same role again to this tool. If not provided, the default role (usually "neondb_owner") will be used.

should_delete_temporary_branch.description: Whether to delete the temporary branch after tuning

temporary_branch_id.description: The ID of the temporary branch that needs to be deleted after tuning.

branch_id.description: The ID or name of the branch that receives the changes. If not provided, the default (main) branch will be used.

name: list_slow_queries
title: List Slow Queries
description: List queries from pg_stat_statements by execution time, slowest first. For sizes, indexes, locks, cache, bloat, or replication use inspect_database.

project_id.description: The ID of the project to list slow queries from

branch_id.description: An optional ID of the branch. If not provided the default branch is used.

database_name.description: The name of the database. If not provided, the default neondb or first available database is used.

compute_id.description: The ID of the compute/endpoint. If not provided, the read-write compute associated with the branch will be used.

limit.description: Maximum number of slow queries to return

min_execution_time.description: Minimum execution time in milliseconds to consider a query as slow

name: inspect_database
title: Inspect Database
description: Run one read-only neon inspect db check (pick `check` from the input schema). Not for arbitrary SQL (`run_sql`), one statement's plan (`explain_sql_statement`), or applying indexes (`prepare_query_tuning`). Omit `database_name` to cover every database; some checks are compute-wide. If a check needs an extension, the tool names `CREATE EXTENSION`; ask before running it.

check.description:
Which diagnostic to run:
`table-sizes`: Size of each table (including TOAST), largest first (pg_table_size)
`index-sizes`: Size of each index, largest first (pg_relation_size)
`unused-indexes`: Non-unique indexes with fewer than 50 scans — candidates for removal (pg_stat_user_indexes)
`seq-scans`: Number of sequential scans recorded against each table (pg_stat_user_tables)
`long-running-queries`: Queries running longer than 5 minutes (pg_stat_activity)
`stalled-queries`: Active queries running longer than 30 seconds with parallel-worker grouping, waits, and blockers, oldest query group first (compute-wide)
`locks`: Locks held with the acquiring query and its age (pg_locks + pg_stat_activity)
`outliers`: The 25 queries with the highest cumulative execution time since statistics were last reset (needs pg_stat_statements)
`calls`: The 25 most frequently executed queries since statistics were last reset (needs pg_stat_statements)
`lfc-hit-rate`: Local File Cache hit rate (compute-wide, needs neon extension)
`working-set`: Estimated working set vs LFC size (compute-wide, needs neon extension)
`vacuum-stats`: Autovacuum status per table: last (auto)vacuum, dead tuples, threshold
`bloat`: Estimated bloat for the 25 most bloated tables (statistical estimate, no extension needed)
`replication-slots`: Replication slots (compute-wide): kind, status, client, restart/confirmed-flush LSNs, and lag (pg_replication_slots + pg_stat_replication)
`subscriptions`: Per-table logical replication progress on this subscriber (pg_subscription_rel)

project_id.description: The ID of the project to inspect

branch_id.description: An optional ID of the branch. If not provided the default branch is used.

database_name.description: For a database-scoped check, the database to inspect. Omit to cover every database on the branch. Ranking and SQL row limits stay per database. One failing database fails the whole run. For a compute-wide check, the database to connect through; the check still runs once for the whole compute and the result does not include `databaseName`. The response `limit` applies to the combined rows after that.

compute_id.description: The ID of the compute/endpoint. If not provided, the read-write compute associated with the branch will be used.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return from the combined result. Per-database ranking and SQL caps are applied first. The response reports how many rows the check produced and whether they were truncated, so raise this only when `truncated` is true. A few checks are capped in SQL and say so in their description.

name: search
title: Search
description: Search across all organizations, projects, and branches by keyword. Returns matching items with id, title, and URL. Query must be at least 3 characters. Do not use when you need all projects (use `list_projects` instead) or to search Neon documentation (use `search_docs`).

query.description: The search query to find matching organizations, projects, or branches

name: fetch
title: Fetch
description: Fetch detailed information about a specific organization, project, or branch using the ID returned by the `search` tool.

id.description: The ID returned by the search tool to fetch detailed information about the entity

name: search_docs
title: Search Documentation
description: Search neon.com: docs, API reference, PostgreSQL tutorial, guides, FAQs, changelog, and blog. Returns ranked pages with title, URL, the matching section, and a slug; read a full page with get_doc.

query.description: What to search for, in words, e.g. "reset a branch" or "connection pooling".

categories.description: Only return pages in these categories: docs, api (API reference), postgresql (PostgreSQL tutorial), guides, faqs, blog, changelog. Omit to search everything.

limit.description: Maximum number of pages to return (1-40).

name: get_doc
title: Get Documentation Page
description: Fetch one neon.com page as markdown. Pass the slug of a search_docs hit (for example docs/guides/prisma).

slug.description: The slug of a hit returned by search_docs, e.g. 'docs/guides/prisma' or 'postgresql/tutorial/inner-join'.

name: send_feedback
title: Send Feedback
description: Send anonymous feedback about Neon or this MCP server to the Neon team. Only call this when the user asks to give feedback. Sends only the feedback text, not account, project, or connection details.

feedback.description: The feedback to send to Neon. Do not include passwords, API keys, connection strings, or other secrets.

name: list_incidents
title: List Neon Incidents
description: List open Neon incidents and maintenance from neonstatus.com, and which components and regions are not operational. Needs no credentials. Call it when Neon requests fail unexpectedly or the user asks whether Neon is down. Incident names can be ticket ids; latest_update carries the details.

name: list_projects
title: List projects
description: List Neon projects you own. Returns every page. Pass limit to cap how many. There is no `cursor` argument. `org_id` is optional: organization API keys use their organization; personal API keys auto-select when unambiguous and otherwise return the IDs to choose from.

limit.description: Specify a value from 1 to 400 to limit number of projects in the response.

timeout.description: Specify an explicit timeout in milliseconds to limit response delay.

recoverable.description: Show only deleted projects within the recovery window.

name: count_projects
title: Retrieve projects count
description: Returns the number of active projects you can access in an organization, without listing them. `org_id` is optional: organization API keys use their organization; personal API keys auto-select when unambiguous and otherwise return the IDs to choose from.

org_id.description: Count projects in the organization with this `org_id`.

name: describe_project
title: Retrieve project details
description: Retrieves the project record (settings, compute, usage). Call `list_branches` for branches.

name: create_project
title: Create project
description: Creates a Neon project and waits until the default compute is ready. `org_id` is optional: organization API keys use their organization; personal API keys auto-select when unambiguous and otherwise return the IDs to choose from. Does not return a connection string; call `get_connection_string` with the project id.

compute_time_seconds.description: The total amount of CPU seconds allowed to be spent by the project's compute endpoints.

written_data_bytes.description: Total amount of data written to all of a project's branches.

data_transfer_bytes.description: Total amount of data transferred from all of a project's branches using the proxy.

logical_size_bytes.description: Limit on the logical size of every project's branch.

allowed_ips.description: A list of IP addresses that are allowed to connect to the compute endpoint.

enable_logical_replication.description: Sets wal_level=logical for all compute endpoints in this project.

weekdays.description: A list of weekdays when the maintenance window is active.

start_time.description: Start time of the maintenance window, in the format of "HH:MM".

end_time.description: End time of the maintenance window, in the format of "HH:MM".

preload_libraries.description: The shared libraries to preload into the project's compute instances.

allowed_origins.description: The browser origins allowed to connect, each `http` or `https` with a host and optional port and no path.

realtime.description: Enable Realtime for the default branch with these options.

name.description: The default branch name.

database_name.description: The database name.

annotations.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata to attach to the branch.

branch.description: Configuration for the initial branch created with the project.

pg_settings.description: A raw representation of Postgres settings

pgbouncer_settings.description: Deprecated. Use the endpoint-level connection pooler configuration instead.

autoscaling_limit_max_cu.description: Default maximum number of Compute Units for endpoints created under this account.

suspend_timeout_seconds.description: Scale-to-zero idle timeout, in seconds, before the compute suspends.

store_passwords.description: Whether or not passwords are stored for roles in the Neon project.

history_retention_seconds.description: History window (point-in-time restore range) for all branches, in seconds.

org_id.description: ID of the organization that will own the project.

name: delete_project
title: Delete project
description: Delete a Neon project and all its data. NEVER run autonomously; always ask the user first. For a single branch, use `delete_branch`.

name: recover_project
title: Recover a deleted project
description: Recovers a deleted project within the 7-day deletion recovery period.

name: list_project_permissions
title: List project access
description: Retrieves details about users who have access to the project, including the permission `id`, the granted-to email address, and the date project access was granted.

name: list_project_members
title: List org members and their project roles
description: Lists organization members and their per-project roles for an org-owned project. Returns every page. Pass limit to cap how many.

limit.description: The maximum number of members to return in the response

annotations.title: List org members and their project roles

name: list_regions
title: List regions
description: Lists Neon regions available to the authenticated account.

name: list_operations
title: List operations
description: Lists operations for a project. Omitting `limit` returns every remaining page. There is no `cursor` argument.

limit.description: Specify a value from 1 to 1000 to limit number of operations in the response

name: get_operation
title: Retrieve operation details
description: Retrieves details for the specified operation.

name: get_project_consumption
title: Retrieve project consumption metrics
description: Returns consumption metrics per project in an organization, grouped by billing period. Omitting `project_ids` returns every project with history in the organization, including deleted ones; pass `project_ids` to narrow it. Requires a Launch, Scale, Agent, Business, or Enterprise plan; other plans return HTTP 403. `metrics` is required, one or more of `compute_unit_seconds`, `root_branch_bytes_month`, `child_branch_bytes_month`, `instant_restore_bytes_month`, `public_network_transfer_bytes`, `private_network_transfer_bytes`, `functions_active_capacity_microseconds`, `functions_waiting_capacity_microseconds`, `functions_invocations`, `functions_egress_bytes`, `extra_branches_month`, `snapshot_storage_bytes_month`; unknown names return no data instead of an error. `org_id` is required; call `list_organizations` for it. `from` and `to` are UTC date-times rounded to `granularity`: `hourly` reaches back 168 hours, `daily` 60 days, `monthly` one year. Returns every page. Pass `limit` to cap how many. There is no `cursor` argument. For per-branch numbers, call `get_branch_consumption`.

limit.description: Maximum number of projects per page.

project_ids.description: Optional project IDs to filter the response (up to 100).

from.description: Specify the start `date-time` for the consumption period.

to.description: Specify the end `date-time` for the consumption period.

granularity.description: Specify the granularity of consumption metrics.

metrics.description: Required. List the metrics to return.

name: get_branch_consumption
title: Retrieve branch consumption metrics
description: Returns consumption metrics per branch for the 1 to 100 projects in `project_ids`, grouped by billing period. Pass `branch_ids` to narrow it. Requires a usage-based Launch, Scale, Agent, or Enterprise plan; other plans return HTTP 403. `metrics` is required, one or more of `compute_unit_seconds`, `root_branch_bytes_month`, `child_branch_bytes_month`, `instant_restore_bytes_month`, `public_network_transfer_bytes`, `private_network_transfer_bytes`, `functions_active_capacity_microseconds`, `functions_waiting_capacity_microseconds`, `functions_invocations`, `functions_egress_bytes`; any other name returns HTTP 400. `extra_branches_month`, `snapshot_storage_bytes_month` are per-project only, on `get_project_consumption`. `org_id` is required; call `list_organizations` for it. `from` and `to` are UTC date-times rounded to `granularity`: `hourly` reaches back 168 hours, `daily` 60 days, `monthly` one year. Returns every page. Pass `limit` to cap how many. There is no `cursor` argument.

limit.description: Maximum number of branches per page.

branch_ids.description: Optional branch IDs to filter the response (up to 100).

from.description: Specify the start `date-time` for the consumption period.

to.description: Specify the end `date-time` for the consumption period.

granularity.description: Specify the granularity of consumption metrics.

metrics.description: Required. List the metrics to return.

name: list_branches
title: List branches
description: Retrieves a list of branches for the specified project. Returns every page. Pass limit to cap how many.

sort_order.description: Defines the sorting order of entities.

limit.description: The maximum number of records to be returned in the response

include_deleted.description: If true, return recoverable deleted branches too (soft-deleted within the recovery window).

name: get_branch
title: Retrieve branch details
description:
Retrieves information about the specified branch.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

name: create_branch
title: Create branch
description: Creates a branch with a read-write compute and waits until it is ready. Pass `no_compute: true` to skip the endpoint. Does not return a connection string; call `get_connection_string` with the project and branch id. Copies the parent at HEAD; point-in-time restore is `restore_snapshot`.

name.description: The branch name

suspend_timeout_seconds.description: Duration of inactivity in seconds after which the compute endpoint is automatically suspended.

compute.description: Autoscaling limits and suspend timeout for the read-write endpoint.

no_compute.description: Skip the read-write endpoint. Default false. Cannot be combined with compute.

name: update_branch
title: Update branch
description:
Updates the specified branch.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

name.description: New display name for the branch.

expires_at.description: The timestamp when the branch is scheduled to expire and be automatically deleted.

name: delete_branch
title: Delete branch
description:
Delete a branch and all its data. NEVER run autonomously; always ask the user first. For the whole project, use `delete_project`.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

name: get_default_branch
title: Get default branch
description: Resolve the project's default branch by the default flag, not by name.

name: set_default_branch
title: Set branch as default
description:
Sets the specified branch as the project's default branch.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

name: reset_from_parent
title: Reset branch from parent
description:
Reset a branch to its parent's current HEAD. Discards every change the branch has written since it diverged. NEVER run autonomously; always ask the user first. `preserve_under_name` saves the current state first and is required when the branch has children; those children move to the new branch. Point-in-time restore is `restore_snapshot`.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

preserve_under_name.description: Name under which to save the current branch before the reset. Required when the branch has children; those children move to the new branch.

name: compare_database_schema
title: Compare database schema
description:
Compare one database's SQL schema on a branch to another. `database_name` is required. Omit `base_branch_id` to compare against the parent; it is a branch id (`br-...`), not a name. Pass `lsn`, `timestamp`, `base_lsn`, or `base_timestamp` only for a point-in-time comparison.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

database_name.description: Name of the database for which the schema is retrieved

base_branch_id.description: The branch ID to compare the schema with

lsn.description: The Log Sequence Number (LSN) for which the schema is retrieved

timestamp.description: The point in time for which the schema is retrieved

base_lsn.description: The Log Sequence Number (LSN) for the base branch schema

base_timestamp.description: The point in time for the base branch schema

name: finalize_branch_restore

name: create_postgres_role

description:
Create a Postgres role on a branch and return it with its password. access defaults to admin: the role joins neon_superuser, so it can read and write every database, create databases and roles, and bypass row-level security, and it cannot be narrowed later. For a least-privilege credential pass access read_only or read_write, scoped to database_name and schemas. Scoped roles are created with SQL as the database owner and cover tables that owner owns, now and later.

database_name.description: Database a read_only or read_write role is scoped to. Optional when the branch has exactly one database.

schemas.description: Schemas a read_only or read_write role can use. Default ["public"].

description:
Adds a social login provider (Google, GitHub, Microsoft, Vercel, Apple) that users sign in with to the branch's Neon Auth integration. Takes the provider `id` and optionally `client_id`, `client_secret` and, for Microsoft, `microsoft_tenant_id`. Microsoft and Apple have no shared app, so they need your own credentials; for Apple, `client_id` is the Services ID, `client_secret` is the `.p8` private key, and `apple_team_id` and `apple_key_id` are required. This is not the OAuth Provider plugin that makes Neon Auth an OAuth 2.1 authorization server; for that use `get_auth_oauth_server` and `update_auth_oauth_server`.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

This is not the OAuth Provider plugin that makes Neon Auth an OAuth 2.1 authorization server; for that use `get_auth_oauth_server` and `update_auth_oauth_server`.

name: get_auth_oauth_server
title: Retrieve OAuth provider plugin configuration
description:
Retrieves how Neon Auth acts as an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the branch, including for MCP servers. This is Better Auth's OAuth Provider plugin (API plugin `oauth_provider`), not social login; for providers such as GitHub or Google call `list_auth_oauth_providers`.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

name: update_auth_oauth_server
title: Update OAuth provider plugin configuration
description:
Configures Neon Auth as an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the branch, including for MCP servers. This is Better Auth's OAuth Provider plugin (API plugin `oauth_provider`), not social login; for providers such as GitHub or Google see `list_auth_oauth_providers`. Enabling requires `login_page`, `consent_page` and at least one resource (or an MCP resource). `resources` replaces the stored list: call `get_auth_oauth_server` first and send the full list to add or remove one. `mcp.resource` is required whenever `mcp` is sent; omitted `mcp` booleans keep their stored value, and `mcp.resource: ""` removes the MCP configuration. Prefer `client_id_metadata_documents` over the deprecated `dynamic_registration`.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

enabled.description: Whether the OAuth provider plugin is enabled.

login_page.description: URL of the page that authorization requests redirect to for sign-in.

consent_page.description: URL of the page that authorization requests redirect to for consent.

resource.description: The MCP server URL that MCP clients (Client ID Metadata Document and dynamically registered) are linked to.

dynamic_registration.description: Whether MCP clients may register themselves via dynamic client registration (RFC 7591).

client_id_metadata_documents.description: Whether MCP clients may identify themselves with an https Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD) URL.

identifier.description: Absolute URL identifying a protected resource.

resources.description: Protected resources that clients can be linked to.

name: list_auth_oauth_clients

name: create_auth_oauth_client
title: Create an OAuth client
description:
Registers an OAuth client with the branch's Neon Auth OAuth server. A confidential client returns `client_secret` only once: show it to the user and tell them to store it. Every entry in `resources` must already be configured on the OAuth server (see `get_auth_oauth_server`) or be its MCP resource. `type` cannot be changed later.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

name.description: Display name of the client.

redirect_uris.description: Redirect URIs the client may use.

type.description: Confidential clients authenticate with a client secret.

resources.description: Identifiers of the protected resources to link the client to.

skip_consent.description: Whether to skip the consent prompt for this client.

name: update_auth_oauth_client
title: Update an OAuth client
description:
Updates an OAuth client of the Neon Auth OAuth server. `redirect_uris` and `resources` replace the stored lists, so send the full list. At least one resource is required. `type` cannot be changed.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

name.description: Display name of the client.

redirect_uris.description: Redirect URIs the client may use.

skip_consent.description: Whether to skip the consent prompt for this client.

resources.description: Identifiers of the protected resources to link the client to.

Deletes an OAuth client from the Neon Auth OAuth server. Irreversible. Tokens already issued to the client are not revoked.

name: update_auth_email_and_password
title: Update email and password configuration
description:
Updates email and password sign-in for the branch's Neon Auth: whether it is enabled, sign-up, email verification, and whether a password reset revokes the user's sessions. Omitted fields keep their value. Call `get_neon_auth_config` to read the current value.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

enabled.description: Controls whether email and password authentication is enabled for this project.

require_email_verification.description: When true, users must verify their email address before they can sign in.

auto_sign_in_after_verification.description: Whether users are automatically signed in after verifying their email

send_verification_email_on_sign_up.description: Whether to send a verification email when users sign up.

send_verification_email_on_sign_in.description: Whether to send a verification email when a user with an unverified email signs in.

name: update_auth_email_provider
title: Update email provider configuration
description:
Sets the email provider Neon Auth sends verification, reset, and invitation emails with. Pass `body.type: "shared"` for Neon's sender, or `body.type: "standard"` with `host`, `port`, `username`, `password`, `sender_email`, and `sender_name` for your own SMTP server. The response omits `password`. Check the server with `send_auth_test_email`.

Sends a test email through the branch's saved SMTP provider (`type: "standard"`) to `recipient_email`. Only send to an address the user gave you. A failed send returns `success: false` with `error_message`, not a tool error.

name: query_logs
title: Query branch logs
description:
Returns logs for a branch. Pass `limit` to cap how many. There is no `cursor` argument. Filters combine with AND. Pass `logql` instead of structured filters, not with them. Give the window as `since` or `start_time`, not both; default is the previous hour, max seven days; `end_time` is exclusive. Private beta; a branch without logs access returns HTTP 404 with reason "telemetry_not_enabled".

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

since.description: A length of time as a count and a unit, for example `30m`, `6h`, or `7d`.

start_time.description: Inclusive beginning of the query window.

end_time.description: Exclusive end of the query window.

limit.description: Maximum number of log records to return per page.

source.description: The Neon service that emitted the log record.

service_name.description: Match the OpenTelemetry `service.name` resource attribute exactly.

scope_name.description: Match the OpenTelemetry instrumentation scope name exactly.

severity_text.description: Match the OpenTelemetry severity text exactly.

body_contains.description: Match records whose rendered `message` contains this case-sensitive substring.

trace_id.description: Match records associated with this OpenTelemetry trace ID.

logql.description: Escape hatch for selections the structured filters cannot express: a raw LogQL expression, evaluated against this branch's log stream.

name: list_log_fields
title: List branch log fields
description:
Lists the low-cardinality log fields observed on this branch. Call `list_log_field_values` with `field_name` to list distinct values.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

name: list_log_field_values
title: List branch log field values
description:
Lists distinct values for a low-cardinality log field. Call `list_log_fields` first for `field_name`; a field the branch has never emitted returns `unknown_field`. Pass `since` or `start_time`, not both; default is the previous six hours, max seven days. Private beta.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

field_name.description: The log field whose distinct values should be returned.

since.description: Length of the lookup window, ending at `end_time` or at the current time when `end_time` is omitted.

start_time.description: Inclusive beginning of the lookup window.

end_time.description: Exclusive end of the lookup window.

source.description: Only consider records emitted by this Neon service.

limit.description: Maximum number of distinct values to return.

name: query_loki_logs
title: Query branch logs (Loki)
description:
Runs a LogQL range query on the branch's Loki-compatible read API and returns Loki's response: `data.result` groups lines by stream labels, and each value is `[nanosecond timestamp string, line]`. Use it for sub-second ordering or stream labels; use `query_logs` for structured filters and one record per line. The source label is `entity_type`; `list_log_fields` and `list_log_field_values` list labels and values. There is no cursor: a result with `limit` lines, or 10,000 (the server's cap, which adds no warning), may be incomplete, so narrow `since` or the selector. Max seven days.

branch_id is a branch id (br-...), not a branch name. Call list_branches to resolve a name.

query.description: LogQL stream selector with optional line filters, e.g. {entity_type="function"} |= "error". The source label is entity_type. No parsers, formatting stages, or metric queries.

since.description: Lookback as a Go duration such as 30m or 24h, ending at end or now. Defaults to 1h. start takes precedence.

start.description: Window start as RFC 3339 or Unix nanoseconds.

end.description: Window end as RFC 3339 or Unix nanoseconds. Defaults to now.

limit.description: Maximum log lines. The server enforces its own cap.
